summary: Taksimo Airport (IATA: TKM) is a small regional airport serving the settlement of Taksimo in the Republic of Buryatia, Russia. Located in the remote northern part of Buryatia near the Muya River valley, it primarily handles short-haul flights connecting this isolated Siberian community with larger regional hubs. The airport plays a vital role in supporting local transportation in an area otherwise accessible mainly by long-distance roads through challenging terrain.
faqs:
Q: What is the airport code for Taksimo Airport?
A: The airport uses the IATA code TKM. It does not have an assigned ICAO code.

Q: Where is Taksimo Airport located?
A: It is situated in Taksimo, a settlement in the Muysky District of the Republic of Buryatia in eastern Siberia, Russia, at coordinates 56.362°N, 114.930°E.

Q: What type of flights operate from Taksimo Airport?
A: The airport primarily handles small regional passenger flights, typically using turboprop aircraft suited to short runways and remote conditions.

Q: How big is Taksimo Airport?
A: It is classified as a small airport with a single runway, serving limited daily traffic and primarily functioning as a local transport link.
transport_tips: Getting to and from Taksimo Airport typically requires a local taxi or pre-arranged vehicle, as public transport options are minimal in this remote settlement. The airport is located close to the town center, making transfers generally quick. Travelers should coordinate ground transport in advance, especially during winter months when weather conditions can affect road travel.
local_tip: If traveling to Taksimo, pack layered clothing regardless of the season—Siberian weather in the Muya valley can swing dramatically, with warm summers giving way to extremely cold winters well below -30°C.
